07:02 Next up we have radial deviation and ulnar deviation. For some of you guys, you've never even heard those terms.

07:11 I'm telling you, for a complete and perfect forearm workout you need to work on these things because there's a reason for them. What we're talking about – radial deviation and ulnar deviation – is how the wrist bends in this frontal plane.

07:20 It's not just about flexion and extension like we talked about. It's also being able to bend this way. So, when we come toward the radius, the top side bone in our forearm here, that's radial deviation.
07:31 Then we go down toward the ulna here, the underside bone of our forearm, that's ulnar deviation. You can see when I do radial deviation here, you see the activity of the muscles of the forearm.

07:41 So why are we not trying to train in that motion? Even though it's small, we need to work on it. And you've probably seen people recommend things you can do for this before. Like, using a sledgehammer.
07:50 And they hold the sledgehammer down at their side to work on radial deviation. They lift the weighted part up in this way. Now what we do is work on the way back.

07:59 For ulnar deviation we flip the sledgehammer around and we lift back that way. Now, the problem is we don't all have sledgehammers. So, what do we do? We can do something in the gym with a rope.
